item.title: Louvre’s Denon Wing Springs a Leak, Damaging One Painting—But the ‘Mona Lisa’ Is Safe
item.description: The leak caused "micro-tears" to a 19th-century French artwork and forced the closure of three galleries.

item.title: Art Investing Startup Masterworks Files Legal Complaint Against an Early Hire Over Lawsuit Threat
item.description: Chief product officer Hai Min Tran says he was illegally fired, while the company maintains that he resigned.

item.title: Staff and Programming Cuts Are Coming to London’s National Gallery Amid Possible $11 M. Deficit
item.description: The $1 billion budgeted for new acquisitions and the $129 million for a 200th anniversary festival were restricted for those purposes.

item.title: Amy Sherald, Ming Smith Among Artworld Figures to Walk the Runway in Carolina Herrera’s Fall 2026 NYFW Show
item.description: “I’m celebrating the kind of women who are often overlooked through history,” said creative director Wes Gordon.

item.title: Wisconsin Museum Treasurer Admits to Stealing $70,000 from Institution
item.description: The Hearthstone Historic House Museum figures in the early history of electric light.

item.title: Trump Wants the National Portrait Gallery to Commission a New Portrait
item.description: Trump wants a portrait that reflects the full scope of his two terms.

item.title: Christie’s to Offer Three Masterworks From Agnes Gund Collection This May
item.description: Long before museums made a point of broadening their collections, Gund was buying work by women and artists of color and urging institutions to do the same.

item.title: University of North Texas Cancels Victor Quiñonez Exhibition, Artist Claims Censorship over Anti-ICE Content in His Work
item.description: The University of North Texas has not released an official reason for the exhibition’s cancelation.

item.title: Adrian Searle to Step Down as the Guardian’s Chief Art Critic After Three Decades
item.description: His final article will run on April 1.

item.title: Louvre Faces €10M Loss After Decades-Long Ticket Fraud Busted
item.description: The Palace of Versailles was also implicated in the scheme, which involved the sale of counterfeit tickets.
